primitives.name: Meta-Variational Random Fourier Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: The kernel is built from random Fourier features z(x) = D^-1/2[cos(ω1Tx+b1),...,cos(ω_DTx+b_D)] where the bases ω are latent variables: q_φ(ω|S) (support-conditioned variational posterior, diagonal Gaussian via 3-layer MLP) approximates p(ω|y,x,S).

reasoning_traces.think:
MetaVRF introduces a variational framework where the random Fourier basis ω is treated as a latent variable, conditioned on task support sets. The variational posterior q_φ(ω|S) approximates the true posterior p(ω|y,x,S) using a diagonal Gaussian distribution. This allows for adaptive kernel construction without requiring full data-driven kernel estimation. The kernel is defined via random Fourier features z(x), which are computed using ω drawn from the variational distribution. The closed-form kernel ridge regression (KRR) base-learner computes weights α = Y(λI + K)^{-1} and predicts Ŷ = αK̃, enabling fast inference without gradient updates. The LSTM module accumulates cross-task context into hidden states h^t, which inform the next task’s variational posterior q_φ(ω^t|h^t). The ELBO objective balances likelihood and KL divergence, encouraging both accurate prediction and compact representation of ω. This architecture supports few-shot learning by adapting kernel structure rapidly to new tasks while maintaining computational efficiency.
